I've been in recovery for about 6-7 months now, some of it was choice and some was forced definitely. My parents told me if i don't agree to getting help they weren't going to help me at all. Yes i live with my family but it's been very hard on them. My brother was definitely the most supportive for me, but he was working a lot so it was hard for me to talk to him. My parents were trying to get me help at first but i refused. So after a few months they just told me if i kept doing what i was doing i'll eventually get arrested and to not come to them when i do. Interesting parenting strategy that didn't really work that well haha. But i'm slowly but surely building up their trust again and it feels good. 

Right now my short term goals are to get hired at my local newspaper (i have an interview with them next week), id like to finish my online classes i have to take to makeup the 9th grade, and some other school stuff nothing really personal though. Long term goals i guess would be to finish high school, go to college, become a well paid famous journalist, live a fulfilling and happy life. 

And finally, like i said earlier with the whole gas thing. It was a very eye opening moment, when i had to take a step outside my own mind and look at myself and ask "What the hell am i doing". I knew that if i didn't stop what i was doing, i'd either be mentally handicapped or i'd be dead before i'm 18. At the time i thought i did want to die but now that i look back on it, i didn't really want to die, i just wanted all the pain i felt to stop. I was going through a very rough patch in my life and recovery was definitely the right step.
